guard: the peer-facing cotal_spawn tool exposes a kickoff prompt and carries it through MeshAgent.spawn into the manager's spawn command
why: The live defect crossed two forwarding seams and one published schema. A new session joined
the roster and received a claude/channel notification, but no first model turn began because
cotal_spawn had no prompt field even though the manager already accepted one.
A1 drops the connector-core to manager handoff. A2 leaves MeshAgent correct but drops the
peer-facing tool's handoff. A3 leaves both implementations intact while hiding the argument
from every MCP host. Each is independently the same user-visible failure, so each has its own
named cell rather than relying on one end-state assertion to guess which seam disappeared.

mutations.name: A1 drop the kickoff prompt at the manager command boundary
mutations.find: const args = { name, role, agent: opts?.agent, model: requested || undefined, variant: opts?.variant, launchOptions: opts?.launchOptions, cwd: opts?.cwd, prompt: opts?.prompt };
mutations.replace: const args = { name, role, agent: opts?.agent, model: requested || undefined, variant: opts?.variant, launchOptions: opts?.launchOptions, cwd: opts?.cwd };

mutations.name: A2 the MCP tool accepts prompt but silently omits it from MeshAgent.spawn
mutations.find: const reply = await agent.spawn(name, role, { agent: agentType, model, variant, launchOptions, cwd, prompt });
mutations.replace: const reply = await agent.spawn(name, role, { agent: agentType, model, variant, launchOptions, cwd });
mutations.expectRed: cotal_spawn tool forwards the kickoff prompt

mutations.name: A3 hide prompt from the published MCP schema
mutations.find:
prompt: z
          .string()
          .min(1)
          .optional()
          .describe(

          ),
mutations.expectRed: cotal_spawn schema exposes the kickoff prompt
